title: Fig: Ancient Figs You Can Visit
meta_description: Figs too wide to measure as a single trunk. The Millennium Tree of Balete Park in the Philippines is a strangler fig you can stand inside.
intro: A fig this size stops being a single trunk and becomes a structure. Nago's Hinpun Gajumaru is the clearest case: its aerial roots fused into a mass nearly 12 metres around, old enough to have gradually swallowed a pine growing beside it. The Philippine balete is a strangler fig that starts in another tree's branches and replaces it; the Millennium Tree in Maria Aurora is a cage of fused roots around a hollow you can stand inside, and on Siquijor a spring rises at the roots of the Enchanted Balete of Lazi. Rio de Janeiro's fig on Rua Faro became the city's first landmarked tree in 1980, after neighbours stood under it to stop a construction crew. Alicante's is wrapped in fireproof tarps every June before the plaza around it is set alight for the Fogueres festival. None has been keyed to an exact species.
